bias.label: Leaning down below 3,745; hawkish Fed minutes pushed gold to a new low

event: No confirmed high-impact event found for Thu 19 Nov (UNVERIFIED). Next Fed decision 8-9 Dec.

bullets.title: New 14-month low
bullets.text: Spot gold traded about 3,720 after the Fed minutes, down more than 3% on the day and the lowest since September 2025.

bullets.title: Minutes were hawkish
bullets.text: Some Fed officials argued for a quarter-point hike in October, and a couple raised a bigger hike.

bullets.title: Inflation is the worry
bullets.text: Most officials see upside risks to inflation from energy prices and supply limits, so markets still expect a hike by year-end.

bullets.title: Hike nearly priced
bullets.text: Before the minutes, odds of a December quarter-point hike were about 95-96%; odds after the minutes are UNVERIFIED.

bullets.title: Dollar still firm
bullets.text: The dollar index is about 103.8, near a 19-month high, and the 10-year yield is about 5.07% (quote time UNVERIFIED).

bullets.title: Big weekly drop
bullets.text: Gold has lost more than 8% in a week, so sharp bounces can happen even in a downtrend.

look: This is counter-trend. The bias is down, so use half size or skip it.

A 15M close back above 3,640 after the dip.

watch: Catching a falling knife. Do not buy at 3,720 just because gold fell 3% today; wait for the zone and a hold.
A 1H close under 3,615 means the bottom failed. Step aside.
Hawkish Fed speakers or strong US data can push the dollar and yields higher and break support fast.
Moving your stop lower when price gets close. That is how a small loss becomes a big one.
